claim_audit_results.claim_summary: Fellowship closes a named competence gap (Bayesian/probabilistic modelling, spatio-temporal AI, sensor-domain transfer, UQ, domain adaptation, operational decision evaluation).
Career progression Plant Physiologist/Agronomist to EO/Geospatial Crop Scientist to independent researcher in transferable agricultural intelligence.
Career Development Plan is D1.3, due M3, owned by fellow and supervisor, signed by both supervisors and fellow.
CDP agreed by M3 and reviewed at five steering points (M6, M12, M16, M20, M27).
CDP comprises six components: research objectives O1-O6, training/career needs, transferable skills, teaching, publications, Open Science.
KPI for CDP agreed by M3 and reviewed at all five steering points traces to D1.3.
Eleven host-to-fellow competences delivered as supervised practice plus named ELTE courses.
Supervision cadence: weekly one-to-ones, weekly co-supervisor technical sessions tapering to monthly, monthly written record, quarterly CDP reviews.
Seven transferable-skill strands embedded in the plan.
Training measures satisfy call requirement SR-04 (transferable/digital skills, Open Science, research integrity).
Open Science operationalised with named open outputs (protocols, manifests, methodology, code, model cards, FAIR metadata, OA publications).
Teaching transfers a five-year university strength into new discipline/institution/language; ELTE MSc module unit and PhD field-experiment co-supervision.
Bidirectional knowledge transfer host<->fellow, delivering EO-02 inter-sectoral/interdisciplinary mind-sets.
Publications organised around four principal outputs P1-P4, >=2 peer-reviewed submissions during/shortly after fellowship.
One public field demonstration with AgroVIR farmers and one public-facing article per year; science communication a transferable-skill strand.
Six-month non-academic placement at AgroVIR over M25-M30 in Hungary.
Placement supplies the inter-sectoral half of the career profile (operational AI evaluation, research-to-MVP translation, commercial requirements exposure).
Non-academic placement is integral, justified and evaluable with explicit career added value per call SR-06.
Placement work content is training-oriented (pipeline hardening, nine-dimension assessment producing D5.4, FMIS roadmap, requirements/user testing).
On-site placement supervision provided at senior research grade (title 'Senior research officer').

Single-researcher fellowship with DEC led by the fellow with ELTE and partners.

European Fellowship with a six-month non-academic placement extension at AgroVIR.
30-month action, M1-M24 at ELTE plus placement M25-M30 at AgroVIR.

Core findings disseminated via peer-reviewed open-access publications, timed with output releases.
Publications organised around four principal outputs P1-P4 with >=2 peer-reviewed submissions.

Predictive engine/model card released with model card; Adaptation protocol states minimum calibration volume.

claim_audit_results.claim_summary: DEC/IP plan responds to prior submission criticism that economic/technological route and IP strategy were insufficiently substantiated (§2.2 ¶233).
Results persist via released engine/model card, FMIS roadmap, open transfer library/adaptation protocol, ELTE teaching, and reviewed CDP.
Integration of results into ELTE teaching carries knowledge into education (EI-06).
DEC measures tied to deliverables and KPIs (D2.2 verdicts, D3.2 model card, D5.4 nine dimensions, D5.5 interfaces/steps).
Measures deliver EI-02/EI-05 via mapped deliverables, EI-03 via activities, contribute to EI-06 and reinforce EI-01.
Transferability-based evaluation framework plus a proximal-hyperspectral-to-Sentinel methodological bridge, with impact beyond crop/region.
Contributes to EU water savings via improved irrigation timing/prioritisation; refuses a pre-committed % reduction, quantifies from evidence.
Water scarcity causes yield losses and higher costs; processing tomato is a high-value test case where timing has agronomic/economic relevance.
Advances a desktop prototype to a validated web MVP externally evaluated by AgroVIR against real agricultural-software requirements.
MATE-MVCRI architecture investigates cross-environment transferability of agricultural AI across Europe.
~30% of EU territory affected by seasonal water scarcity in an average year, with yield losses, higher costs, rising irrigation demand.
Action delivers research-to-operation path OC5: externally evaluated web MVP plus named post-MSCA FMIS route.
DrR web MVP delivered at M24, before the placement window.
AgroVIR functional/technical evaluation covers all nine assessment dimensions.
FMIS integration roadmap names required interfaces and post-fellowship embedding steps.
Transfer library records a transferable-or-hyperspectral-only verdict for every candidate feature.
One model card published for the released FIELDWISE predictive engine.
Forecast horizons t+1, t+3, t+5 each reported with calibration and prediction-interval coverage.
Field Decision Value computed for >=2 competing models with lead time, false-action rate, missed-stress rate.
Adaptation protocol states minimum local-calibration volume, bounding cost of geographic reuse.
Hungary->Bulgaria transferability report reports zero-shot and calibrated performance, delivered to Prof. Vinelina Yankova at MVCRI.
Open-access dissemination of transferability paradigm/sensor-domain method contributes to enriched cross-boundary European R&I culture (EI-02).
Reusable, uptake-ready outputs strengthen R&I capacity/output/knowledge-transfer of participating organisations (EI-05).
Recurring public-engagement activities broaden public understanding of transferable agricultural AI (EI-03).
At least two high-quality peer-reviewed open-access submissions targeted during/shortly after the fellowship.
Magnitude expressed through eleven KPIs each tracing to a named deliverable, making impact claims evaluator-verifiable.
